newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude firmer, Minas traded premium doubles.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude firmer, Minas traded premium doubles.

text.p: Asian crude prices were firmer on Thursday as futures prices rebounded and worries about tighter supplies of Minas in June doubled the crude's premium.
A U.S. major sold 100,000 to 150,000 barrels of June Minas to a trader at ICP +30 cents, while a 100,000-barrels parcel changed hands in Japan at the same premium, traders said on Thursday.

That doubles the premium seen in the latest deals. Earlier this week, a U.S. major sold 100,000 barrels to a Japanese refinery at +15 cents and a second deal for 150,000 barrels was done at the same level.

Traders said worries that Pertamina would reduce the June export allocations of Minas to feed the new 60,000 barrels per day (bpd) crude unit at the 250,000 bpd Balikpapan refinery was behind the rise in the price.

The new unit is to start testing crudes, initially Minas, from next week, traders said. Two smaller crude units will be mothballed, but traders said it was not clear if they would be mothballed permanently or temporarily.
Traders said they would expect sellers to now target 30 to 35 cents premium, subject to a low allocation of Minas crude from Pertamina.
In the Middle East market, an overhang of Oman and Murban continued to dog the market's footsteps.
Traders said one major refiner might be sitting on as much as 1.5 million barrels of Oman, and the Oman government might be looking to sell the same amount too.
Murban was said to be in plentiful supply also.
